## Historical audit — S0169

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_16007442/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines; observations were not split across chunks.

| Area | Evidence and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Goal | The instruction was to reconstruct an indoor photograph with separate 3D geometry and matching camera and framing; no calibration or other views were available (student request, line 1). The student’s code interpreted the scene as an electronics workbench. That interpretation is not independent verification of the unseen reference image. |
| Scene construction | The programs specify many objects, including walls, bench, monitor, oscilloscope, meters, cabinets, cables and tools; they use colored materials and roughness, but no image texture is evident. Asset grouping and explicit coordinates express intended part relationships and rotations, including a tilted meter. Neither physical connection nor pose accuracy is geometrically verified (student responses, lines 3, 8 and 13). |
| First correction | Step 1 failed because the mouse fillet radius exceeded half its smallest dimension; no image was returned (execution result, line 5). After receiving that traceback, the student reduced the radius from .027 to .020, changed the camera and replaced the holder with a continuous coil; the revised program was executed (request line 6; response line 8; execute line 9). |
| Timeout and revision | Step 2 timed out after approximately 600 seconds, with empty stdout and stderr and no image (line 10). The student then batched small details, used Blender curves for wires, removed per-object modifiers and reduced Cycles samples from 32 to 16; step 3 executed that revision (response line 13; execute line 14). These are observable efficiency changes, not proof of the timeout’s cause. |
| Final visible result | Step 3 reached world setup but failed because `scene.world` was `None`; no image was returned (line 15). With zero executions remaining, the student returned another complete program that creates a world if absent (request line 16; response line 18). No execution of that last correction is visible. |

**Validation and outcome.** All three recorded execution results were unsuccessful, so there is no visible successful build, render comparison, formal success, or independent evidence of partial visual correctness. The observed outcome is an initial construction error, a technical timeout, and a subsequent build error; the final correction is untested. Camera, lighting, framing, occlusion, materials, part connections and object poses therefore remain unverified. Whether scene complexity caused the timeout is unresolved.

**Input and exploration.** This is a student trajectory, not a teacher-only trace. No teacher detection, diagnosis, recommendation, receipt or adoption appears. The actual feedback was runner error output delivered in subsequent student requests. The student autonomously revised programs between runs; recorded student sessions report zero tool calls (lines 2, 7, 12 and 17). No rendered image was available for the requested visual review.

**Lessons.** Transferable observations are that primitive parameter limits and nullable scene setup can prevent rendering, and that a timeout alone does not identify its bottleneck. The fillet dimensions, workbench arrangement and proposed batching are specific to this attempt; their visual effectiveness remains a hypothesis.
